comments.author: theasianpianist
comments.body:
It looks like the root cause of this is `ndppd` loading IPv6 routes every 30 seconds: https://github.com/DanielAdolfsson/ndppd/blob/b8b2d401b9a83dae45776bb9fa95b1a5fe417d01/src/route.cc#L129

Because of all the routes announced by the T1s, the `/proc/net/ipv6_route` file is about 24k lines long. In `top`, `ndppd` CPU usage can be seen spiking every 30s (lasting for 7-8 seconds) which also corresponding with the debug logs generated on this line https://github.com/DanielAdolfsson/ndppd/blob/b8b2d401b9a83dae45776bb9fa95b1a5fe417d01/src/route.cc#L86

It does not look like there is a way to prevent `ndppd` from reading the IPv6 routes since that is part of its core feature set. However, there is theoretically a way to increase the polling interval so that the CPU spikes happen less frequently. The documentation is either out of date or incorrect, so I am investigating further along this avenue.

comments.author: theasianpianist
comments.body: After further investigation, the `route-ttl` configuration option can be used to change how frequently kernel IPv6 routes are read. Since this value is stored internally as a [signed integer](https://github.com/DanielAdolfsson/ndppd/blob/b8b2d401b9a83dae45776bb9fa95b1a5fe417d01/src/route.cc#L27), we can delay the CPU spikes to once every 2147483647ms (about 24 days) at most.

Fixes #6823 

#### Why I did it
`ndppd` by default reads `/proc/net/ipv6_route` ever 30 seconds. Since T1s advertise so many routes to ToRs, this file is extremely large, and reading it causes `ndppd`'s CPU usage to spike every 30 seconds

#### How I did it
Increase the delay for reading this file to the maximum possible value (max integer value), which will result in CPU spikes every ~24 days instead of every 30 seconds

#### How to verify it
Start `ndppd` with the new config file, confirm that no CPU spikes are seen except at startup
